title: "Predicting inpatient length of stay for patients with diabetes"
author: "Richard Mali"
output:
  github_document:
    html_preview: false

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, fig.align = "center")
source("../R/utils.R")
for (f in list.files(repo_path("R"), pattern = "[.]R$", full.names = TRUE)) source(f)
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(caret))
started <- Sys.time()
threads <- n_threads()
seed <- 5330
```

This notebook fits five regression models for `time_in_hospital` (days, 1 to 14)
in the UCI Diabetes 130-US Hospitals data and evaluates them once on held-out
patients. Rare-level lumping, median imputation, scaling and the k-means
care-complexity cluster are all fit on training patients only.

## 1. Data and cohort

```{r load}
raw <- data.table::fread(repo_path("data", "diabetic_data.csv.gz"), data.table = FALSE,
                         na.strings = c("", "NA", "?"))
n_encounters <- nrow(raw)
n_patients <- length(unique(raw$patient_nbr))
repeat_share <- mean(duplicated(raw$patient_nbr))

n_invalid_gender <- sum(first_encounter_per_patient(raw)$gender %in% "Unknown/Invalid")
analytic <- prepare_los(raw)
rf_trees <- 200
if (quick_run()) {
  set.seed(seed)
  analytic <- analytic[sample(nrow(analytic), 6000), ]
  rf_trees <- 50
}
n_analytic <- nrow(analytic)
```

The raw file has `r fmt_int(n_encounters)` encounters from `r fmt_int(n_patients)`
patients; `r fmt_pct(repeat_share)` of encounters are repeat visits by a patient
already in the data. In the course version, encounters were split at random, so
the same patient could appear in both training and test data. Repeat stays of one
person share diagnoses, medications and care patterns, so that split rewards a
model for recognizing patients rather than for generalizing to new ones, and it
also makes CV folds within the training set leak in the same way.

Here I keep each patient's first encounter (lowest `encounter_id`) and drop the
`r n_invalid_gender`
first encounters with gender recorded as Unknown/Invalid. The analytic cohort has
`r fmt_int(n_analytic)` patients, one row each, so a random split is a split by
patient. Mean length of stay is `r fmt_num(mean(analytic$time_in_hospital), 2)` days
(median `r median(analytic$time_in_hospital)`).

Coding notes (`R/recode_hospital.R`): `?` is missing; missing race is kept as a
`Missing` level; age bands such as `[70-80)` become midpoints (75);
`max_glu_serum` and `A1Cresult` of `None` mean the test was not done and become
`Not_measured`; admission type, discharge disposition and admission source are
ID codes treated as categories.

## 2. Train/test split and train-only preprocessing

```{r split}
set.seed(seed)
train_idx <- createDataPartition(analytic$time_in_hospital, p = 0.80, list = FALSE)[, 1]
lumped <- lump_rare_levels(analytic[train_idx, ], analytic[-train_idx, ],
                           vars = los_factor_vars, min_n = 30)
prep <- fit_preprocessor(lumped$train, impute_vars = los_numeric_vars,
                         cluster_vars = los_numeric_vars,
                         cluster_name = "care_complexity_cluster", k = 3, nstart = 20,
                         seed = seed)
train <- apply_preprocessor(prep, lumped$train)
test <- apply_preprocessor(prep, lumped$test)

base_predictors <- c(los_numeric_vars, los_factor_vars)
predictors <- c(base_predictors, "care_complexity_cluster")
outcome <- "time_in_hospital"
y_train <- train[[outcome]]
y_test <- test[[outcome]]
train_counts <- lapply(los_factor_vars, function(v) table(analytic[train_idx, v]))
pooled_vars <- los_factor_vars[vapply(train_counts, function(t) any(t > 0 & t < 30), logical(1))]
```

The 80/20 split is stratified on length-of-stay quantiles (train n =
`r fmt_int(nrow(train))`, test n = `r fmt_int(nrow(test))`). Category levels with
fewer than 30 training patients are pooled into `Other` (this affected
`r paste(pooled_vars, collapse = ", ")`), using training counts
only. The care-complexity cluster (k = 3, 20 starts) is fit on standardized age
and the seven utilization counts in the training set; test patients are assigned
to the nearest training center.

```{r cluster-profile}
profile <- cluster_profile(prep, train)
profile$mean_los_train <- round(tapply(y_train, train$care_complexity_cluster, mean)[profile$cluster], 2)
write_table(profile, "los_cluster_profile")
knitr::kable(profile, col.names = c("Cluster", "Age", "Labs", "Procedures", "Medications",
                                    "Outpatient", "Emergency", "Inpatient", "Diagnoses",
                                    "Train n", "Mean LOS"))
```

### PCA check

```{r pca}
pca_x <- model.matrix(reformulate(base_predictors), data = train)[, -1]
pca_x <- pca_x[, apply(pca_x, 2, sd) > 0]
pca <- prcomp(pca_x, center = TRUE, scale. = TRUE)
pca_cum <- cumsum(pca$sdev^2) / sum(pca$sdev^2)
pca_90 <- which(pca_cum >= 0.90)[1]
```

On the dummy-coded training predictors, `r pca_90` of `r length(pca_cum)`
components are needed for 90% of the variance, so I kept the original variables.

## 3. Models and cross-validation

```{r fit}
folds <- cv_folds(y_train, k = 5, seed = seed)
fit_start <- Sys.time()
models <- regression_models(train, outcome, predictors, folds, threads, rf_trees = rf_trees)
models$forest_no_cluster <- fit_ranger_fixed(train, outcome, base_predictors,
                                             tune = models$forest$bestTune, threads = threads,
                                             trees = rf_trees, classification = FALSE)
fit_minutes <- as.numeric(difftime(Sys.time(), fit_start, units = "mins"))
tree_leaves <- sum(models$tree$finalModel$frame$var == "<leaf>")

labels <- c(linear = "Linear regression", ridge = "Ridge", lasso = "Lasso",
            tree = "Regression tree", forest = "Random forest",
            forest_no_cluster = "Random forest, no cluster")
colors <- model_colors(unname(labels[c("linear", "ridge", "lasso", "tree", "forest")]))
cv_names <- c("linear", "ridge", "lasso", "tree", "forest")
cv_table <- data.frame(
  model = labels[cv_names],
  cv_rmse = vapply(models[cv_names], cv_summary, numeric(1), metric = "RMSE"),
  cv_mae = vapply(models[cv_names], cv_summary, numeric(1), metric = "MAE"),
  tuning = vapply(models[cv_names], tune_label, character(1))
)
write_table(cv_table, "los_cv_results")
knitr::kable(transform(cv_table, cv_rmse = fmt_num(cv_rmse), cv_mae = fmt_num(cv_mae)),
             row.names = FALSE, col.names = c("Model", "5-fold CV RMSE", "5-fold CV MAE",
                                              "Selected tuning"))
```

The forest uses `ranger` with `r rf_trees` trees; the no-cluster forest reuses
its tuned settings without the cluster feature. The selected regression tree has
`r fmt_int(tree_leaves)` leaves. Model fitting took `r fmt_num(fit_minutes, 1)`
minutes on `r threads` threads.

## 4. Held-out test performance

```{r test-metrics}
test_pred <- lapply(models, function(m) as.numeric(predict(m, newdata = test)))
test_pred$null <- rep(mean(y_train), nrow(test))
labels <- c(labels, null = "Training mean (no model)")

test_table <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(test_pred), function(m) {
  cbind(model = labels[[m]], regression_metrics(y_test, test_pred[[m]]))
}))
test_table <- test_table[order(test_table$rmse), ]
write_table(test_table, "los_test_metrics")
knitr::kable(transform(test_table, rmse = fmt_num(rmse), mae = fmt_num(mae), r2 = fmt_num(r2)),
             row.names = FALSE, col.names = c("Model", "Test RMSE (days)", "Test MAE (days)",
                                              "Test R-squared"))

best <- names(labels)[match(test_table$model[1], labels)]
diff_best <- paired_rmse_diff(y_test, test_pred[[best]], test_pred$linear, seed = seed)
diff_cluster <- paired_rmse_diff(y_test, test_pred$forest, test_pred$forest_no_cluster,
                                 seed = seed)
comparisons <- rbind(cbind(comparison = paste(labels[[best]], "minus Linear regression"), diff_best),
                     cbind(comparison = "Random forest minus Random forest, no cluster",
                           diff_cluster))
write_table(comparisons, "los_rmse_comparisons", digits = 5)
```

R-squared is computed on the test set as 1 - SSE/SST around the test mean.
Differences in test RMSE, with 95% paired bootstrap intervals (2,000 resamples of
test patients):

```{r comparisons}
knitr::kable(transform(comparisons, diff = fmt_num(diff, 4), low = fmt_num(low, 4),
                       high = fmt_num(high, 4)),
             col.names = c("Comparison", "RMSE difference", "95% CI low", "95% CI high"))
```

```{r observed-predicted}
show_models <- c("linear", "tree", "forest")
op_df <- do.call(rbind, lapply(show_models, function(m) {
  data.frame(model = labels[[m]], observed = y_test, predicted = test_pred[[m]])
}))
op_df$model <- factor(op_df$model, levels = unname(labels[show_models]))
p_op <- plot_observed_vs_predicted(op_df, colors[unname(labels[show_models])],
                                   title = "Predicted vs observed length of stay")
save_figure(p_op, "los_observed_vs_predicted", width = 7, height = 7)
knitr::include_graphics(figure_link("los_observed_vs_predicted"))
```

All models pull predictions toward the mean: short stays are over-predicted and
long stays under-predicted. This is what an R-squared near
`r fmt_num(test_table$r2[1], 2)` looks like in practice.

### Residual diagnostics

```{r residuals}
res_models <- c("linear", "forest")
res_df <- do.call(rbind, lapply(res_models, function(m) {
  data.frame(model = labels[[m]], predicted = test_pred[[m]], residual = y_test - test_pred[[m]])
}))
res_df$model <- factor(res_df$model, levels = unname(labels[res_models]))
p_res <- plot_residuals(res_df, colors[unname(labels[res_models])],
                        title = "Residuals vs predicted length of stay")
save_figure(p_res, "los_residuals", width = 9, height = 4.5)
knitr::include_graphics(figure_link("los_residuals"))

lin_resid <- y_test - test_pred$linear
p_qq <- plot_qq(lin_resid, "Normal Q-Q plot, linear regression test residuals")
save_figure(p_qq, "los_linear_qq", width = 5.5, height = 5)
knitr::include_graphics(figure_link("los_linear_qq"))
resid_skew <- mean((lin_resid - mean(lin_resid))^3) / sd(lin_resid)^3
below_one <- mean(test_pred$linear < 1)
```

The diagonal stripes are there because the outcome is whole days. The linear
model's residual smooth bends at both ends: it under-predicts patients it scores
lowest and over-predicts those it scores highest, and `r fmt_pct(below_one)` of
its test predictions are below one day, which is impossible for an inpatient
stay. The forest's residuals stay centered across the range, which matches its
lower test error. Residuals are also right-skewed (skewness
`r fmt_num(resid_skew, 2)` for the linear model). RMSE and MAE remain valid
accuracy summaries, but normal-theory standard errors for the linear model's
coefficients would not be, so I compare models on test error rather than on
coefficient p-values. A count model (Poisson or negative binomial) is a natural
next step.

## 5. Which predictors matter

Permutation importance here is the increase in test RMSE when one predictor is
shuffled.

```{r importance}
rmse_metric <- function(y, p) sqrt(mean((y - p)^2))
imp_models <- c("linear", "forest")
imp <- do.call(rbind, lapply(imp_models, function(m) {
  pf <- function(d) as.numeric(predict(models[[m]], newdata = d))
  cbind(model = labels[[m]],
        permutation_importance(pf, test, y_test, predictors, rmse_metric,
                               higher_is_better = FALSE, seed = seed))
}))
imp$model <- factor(imp$model, levels = unname(labels[imp_models]))
write_table(imp, "los_permutation_importance", digits = 5)
p_imp <- plot_importance(imp, colors[unname(labels[imp_models])],
                         title = "Predictor importance for length of stay",
                         x_label = "Increase in test RMSE when shuffled (days)")
save_figure(p_imp, "los_permutation_importance", width = 9, height = 5)
knitr::include_graphics(figure_link("los_permutation_importance"))
top_linear <- head(imp$variable[imp$model == labels[["linear"]]], 4)
top_forest <- head(imp$variable[imp$model == labels[["forest"]]], 4)
```

## 6. Summary

- Lowest test RMSE: `r test_table$model[1]`, `r fmt_num(test_table$rmse[1])` days
  (MAE `r fmt_num(test_table$mae[1])`, R-squared `r fmt_num(test_table$r2[1])`),
  versus `r fmt_num(test_table$rmse[test_table$model == labels[["null"]]])` days for
  predicting the training mean.
- The care-complexity cluster changed random forest test RMSE by
  `r fmt_num(diff_cluster$diff, 4)` days (95% CI `r fmt_num(diff_cluster$low, 4)` to
  `r fmt_num(diff_cluster$high, 4)`).
- Top predictors by permutation importance: `r paste(top_linear, collapse = ", ")`
  (linear) and `r paste(top_forest, collapse = ", ")` (random forest).
- Several predictors (number of lab tests, medications, procedures and diagnoses,
  and discharge disposition) are only known during or at the end of the stay. The
  models therefore describe what tracks with longer stays; they are not
  admission-time forecasts.

```{r runtime}
runtime <- as.numeric(difftime(Sys.time(), started, units = "mins"))
```

Notebook runtime: `r fmt_num(runtime, 1)` minutes.
